body: Device secret is a drop-in value of CCTG_HUB_SECRET (cctgd_<id>_<64 hex>), checked by the hub against sha256 in devices.json; hello/Authorization unchanged, no wire VERSION bump, old agents and hooks work with it. Rejected: a new hello field or header carrying device id separately (needs agent/hook changes and a capability flag for nothing).

Join codes minted into <state>/join/<sha256(code)>.json (expiry only) so a separate process (docker compose exec hub cctg hub code) can mint and the hub spends by remove_file (one winner). Rejected: an admin endpoint on the hub for minting (new authenticated surface) and in-memory codes (CLI in another process cannot reach them).

Exchange is POST /v1/join on the hook listener, the only route without Authorization, body <=1 KiB, 403 after the 250 ms auth delay for unknown/used/expired alike; client is a new 'cctg join' subcommand (TLS pin via DeviceConfig) that rewrites the CCTG_HUB_SECRET line of device.env itself. Rejected: curl in install.sh (curl pins SPKI via --pinnedpubkey, our pin is the certificate sha256) and a new line on the agent link (install.sh has no agent).

Code = 16 Crockford base32 chars (80 bits), 10 min, single use; above NIST 800-63B 64-bit floor for unthrottled look-up secrets, so no extra global join limiter (which would let anyone lock joins). Rejected: 8-digit numeric codes (need strict lockout) and 128-bit hex codes (hard to type from a phone).

/devices and its buttons get their own worker (hub/roster.rs) routed in hub::route_inbound before the slots actor, so slots.rs (TASK-053 in flight) is untouched; revoke asks one confirmation. Rejected: handling in slots::press (16k-line actor, merge conflict with TASK-053).

Guard tests/hub_reads_no_files.rs flagged new log strings containing 'device' in ingress.rs: its code_only skipped one char too many after a non-raw opening quote, so an empty string "" swallowed its closing quote and later string contents were scanned as code. Renaming strings would only hide it; fixed the skip (raw strings only) and added "" cases to the guard's self-test. Hub code also avoids the identifier 'device' (forbidden name for crate::device), hence entry/device_id in roster.rs and ingress.rs.

Burst probe (200 simultaneous joins from distinct 127.0.1.x sources) could not tell the join path from the 401 path: Windows loopback backlog capped both at 128 answered; replaced by a two-wave probe (64 bad requests, then 64 more while the first sleep).

Refused join keeps its hook request place through the 250 ms pause (remove drop(permit) in the Route::Join arm), matching the 401 path and TASK-035 limits; alternative rejected: a separate join semaphore (new limit, more code).

Code spent on JoinError::Full stays as in the reference; alternative rejected: checking capacity before take_code, which answers 503 to a wrong code on a full hub (a hint without a valid code) or needs a peek-then-take step.

Main moved on with TASK-053: applied both patches directly (git apply --ignore-whitespace, not --3way) since --check passed; the 4 verify_final MISMATCH files (ingress.rs, wire.rs, install_e2e.rs, install.sh) differ from the 7748a43 reference result exactly by the TASK-053 delta (drift_check.sh). Alternative rejected: hand-merging via --3way.

Verdict SHIP, not NEEDS_WORK: the only revoke gap found is a hook whose headers were authenticated before the revoke and whose body arrives within the 2 s request window (accepted without a recheck); it needs a revoke inside that window and is left as a minor follow-up (one is_active recheck after read_request). Full-suite failures of join_e2e/install_e2e were a stale cctg.exe from another worktree in the shared target; rerun after touch is green.

Review finding 2 fix "refuse unless registry.json/offset exist" rejected: install.sh --hub mints right after the hub starts, and a device ~/.cctg also exists. Chosen: Devices::open creates <state>/join at hub start; mint_code refuses (MintError::NoHub, absolute path in the message) when join/ is missing, never creates it.

take_code serialised by a process-wide mutex: the new race test showed two concurrent remove_file of one code file both return Ok on Windows (handle-based delete), i.e. one code enrolled two devices. Alternative rename-to-claim rejected (also handle-based on Windows). One hub per state dir is the supported setup.

Code lifetime cap uses the code file mtime as mint time: deadline = min(expires, mtime+10min), and a deadline more than 10 min after now counts as expired (clock ran ahead / hand-written file). Alternative expires<=now+TTL+60 alone rejected: it does not bound a file written long ago with a far expiry.
